storm.summary_layperson: A band of rain showers with gusty southwest winds is moving through around 4:30–5 PM — no thunderstorms expected, and the Sound won't make much difference here compared with neighboring towns.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer this evening: the Sound (52°F) is already about 4°F warmer than the air at 4 PM, and the gap widens to ~7°F the wrong way by 7 PM as the air cools — no protection at any point in the window.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: a low-pressure system (barometer near 996 hPa) is pushing showers across the area on a strong southwest flow. Radar shows a scatter of moderate rain cells (35–40 dBZ) within about 30 miles, the whole pattern moving ENE at roughly 36 kt. Several nearby backyard stations in Rye, Port Chester and Old Greenwich have logged 1–2.5 mm of rain in the past hour, so these echoes are real rain, not radar clutter. There is essentially no instability (CAPE 50 J/kg) despite 37 kt of wind shear aloft, so lightning and hail are not expected — this is a showery, gusty evening, not a thunderstorm setup. No NWS alerts are active.

Local modifier — none in play: the cove's usual protection comes from cool Sound water under warmer air, which forms a stable layer that weakens incoming storms. Tonight it's the reverse: the water (52°F) is warmer than the air (~48°F now). After sunset (4:27 PM) the air keeps cooling while the Sound holds its temperature, so the gap moves further in the wrong direction — about −5°F at 5 PM and −7°F by 7 PM. There is no stable layer and no buffer at any point in the window.

The sea breeze is out of the picture too — it's late November, the sun set at 4:27 PM, and the land is no warmer than the water. What the cove does have is a steady onshore southwest wind off the Sound (forecast SSW around 16 kt at 5 PM). That background wind blows against the low-level approach of the showers and gives a small nudge later on the arrival time, but it won't weaken them.

Arrival: the closest cell is about 5 miles WNW of the cove, sliding in slowly; expect it around 4:45 PM (window 4:30–5:00 PM, medium confidence). Expect a burst of rain and gusts into the low 20s kt as it passes, then more scattered showers. Cells to the north and northeast are moving away from the cove.

Cove vs. surrounding areas: essentially the same as Stamford, Rye and the Long Island north shore — passing showers, a raw southwest wind, and stronger gusts out on the open Sound (the mid-Sound buoy is reading 22 kt gusting 31).

What would change the call: echoes intensifying above 45 dBZ near the cove, or an NWS warning, would push this to high risk. With a low this deep, a wind shift to the west or northwest behind a cold front later tonight is possible but is beyond what the model run covers.

arrival.blurb: Radar-tracked shower 5 mi WNW edging toward the cove; no marine-layer buffer tonight, so expect it at full strength — rain and gusts, no thunder.

wind.regime_label: Moderate southwest gradient wind — no sea breeze
wind.tactics_blurb: Realistically no racing — it's dark from 4:30 PM, cold, and showery. If anything is on the water, the southwest breeze channels slightly along the west shore: lean right (west) on the beats.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
The call: a moderate gradient-wind evening, not a sea-breeze day. The wind is being driven by the passing low-pressure system, not by daytime heating. The air–water temperature difference is −3.8°F (the Sound is warmer than the air), so the thermal engine that makes a sea breeze isn't running at all. Across the reliable stations the background wind averages about 12 kt from the southwest (228°), with good agreement between stations.

Will it die at sunset? No. Sunset is 4:27 PM, but a gradient wind doesn't care about the sun. The model has the breeze peaking around 15–16 kt early in the window, then easing to about 13 kt by 7 PM and veering a few degrees from SSW (213°) to SW (223°). Beyond 7 PM the model run doesn't reach, so 8–10 PM are carried forward by persistence with the usual 1–2 kt of softening as the air near the water stabilizes after dark.

Cove numbers: RYC is reading 10 kt gusting 19, with a 10-minute average of 13 kt — almost exactly what the model has for the cove right now, so the forecast speeds are used as-is, not scaled. Out on the open Sound the buoy has 22 kt gusting 31, so it's noticeably windier beyond the cove mouth.

Where the pressure is: in SW–SSW flow the breeze comes cleanly in from the Sound with slight channeling along the west shore (Field Point / Belle Haven side), and is a touch stronger near the mouth. Facing upwind into the southwest, that west shore is the right side of the course — lean right, but don't expect a big edge; this direction is usually fairly even and steady.

Shift character: steady direction with normal gust-and-lull cycling, except when shower cells pass — expect brief gusts into the low 20s and short-lived shifts as they go through, mainly around 4:30–5 PM. With a low this deep, a frontal shift to the west or northwest later tonight is possible but outside the model's reach.

Fleet impact: 12–15 kt with gusts near 20 is full-hike for dinghies and comfortable-to-lively for keelboats — but in the dark, in 48°F air with rain, this is not a racing evening.

data_caveats: Model hourly wind only reaches 7 PM (later forecast hours unavailable); 8, 9 and 10 PM rows are extrapolated by persistence with slight after-dark softening
New London airport (KGON) and one other airport station returned no wind and were excluded from the wind averages
